title: Early Life Exploration
opening: Use evidence already available: a memory, an existing recollection, a record, current behavior, or an unanswered question. You do not need to ask anyone for a new account. Compare examples with present choices. A childhood pattern is a clue, not a fixed identity.

prompts.result: Write what you already know as a short comparison: a specific event or recurring behavior, including interests, aversions, absorption or responses to difficulty if known; its source; what it may suggest; a present choice or other evidence that supports, conflicts with, or cannot answer the idea; and any disagreement or question to examine now. Use events, not trait labels. Leave unknown parts open.

limits.heading: Keep the comparison open
limits.body: No single recollection has to win. Do not force a childhood-to-adult pattern, infer a diagnosis, try to recover an absent memory, or treat its absence as a problem. Current behavior may matter more for a current decision.
limits.privacy: Leave this blank to continue without saving.

feedback.length: This note is over the 2,000-character save limit. Shorten it to save; the full draft remains here.
feedback.missing: Add a note if you want to save, or leave the lesson without saving.
feedback.saveFailure: The save did not finish. Your notes remain here; retry the save.
feedback.retryPending: A save needs a result before editing or starting another save.
feedback.conflict: Another save changed these notes. Your draft remains here; compare it with the saved version before saving again.
